account:
Today has mostly involved my usual appointments, but there is persistent, unverified talk of a change at the bridge or port. Several townsfolk repeated that phrase and associated it with the bakery or inn. One mentioned the baker, freight, and neighbour being present, but nobody gave me a concrete description of a change or a firsthand explanation. The secretary says the neighbour reported that the baker knew of no confirmed changes. I cannot yet say whether anything actually changed, who arranged it, or what it would be for.

I went to the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection but could not find the miller. The baker had also reported being unable to find him earlier. I obtained no grain figures or delivery records, so the inspection is incomplete; his absence alone does not establish a problem. I asked the secretary to request another inspection appointment when she sees him.

The secretary reports that no council letters have arrived. She is keeping the appointment book secure and receiving correspondence at town hall until three, holding letters for my four-thirty return. I have kept my noon lunch and afternoon correspondence appointments, and next have private tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage at three. There is no confirmed public gathering or town bread order that I know of.
